version.author: kallums
version.changelog: ScaleView Pro. A 200x100 icon showing the twelve pitch classes as circles, with the notes of the selected scale lit, the notes you play ringed, and the chord you are holding named underneath. The chord is read rather than looked up, so extended and thin voicings are named instead of being read out as notes. Note names are spelled for the key - Gb major reads Gb Ab Bb Cb Db Eb F - with a Simplify Note Names option for piano-key naming. 18 spelled roots against 16 scale types. The scale is remembered per project, and a toolbar button lights up while the script runs.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Wording in the menus follows Apple's writing guidelines: "Random Scale" is now "Choose a Random Scale". Also the first release of everything since 1.0.3: the house colours (a darker background, a yellow ring round a played note, White in place of Gold among the highlights); a played note always lights up straight away; a doubled root of the key reads as root position (E G C C is C, not C/E); altered dominants keep their root (C7#5b9 reads Caug7b9); a draw goes to the name without a slash (C D G Bb is C7sus2); Starting Blocks' chords decide which roots a chord can have; and no MIDI is dropped however busy the input.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Easier to read and reachable from the keyboard, after Apple's design guidelines: note names on circles outside the key are now light on a darker circle (8:1 contrast, was 3:1); no text is smaller than 10 points, so a very small icon shows the circles without names; S or Return opens the scale list and O the options.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Easier to see and in your system's typeface, after Apple's design guidelines: circles outside the scale keep their dark fill but get a thin lighter rim, so every note's place shows (3:1 contrast, was 1.4:1); note names and the label use San Francisco on a Mac or Segoe UI on Windows where REAPER can find them, Arial otherwise.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Chords are named by ScaleView's own reading again, not checked against Starting Blocks' chord list. That list held only complete chords, so a chord played with a note left out was often named on the wrong root: C D E G A B now reads Cmaj13 (was Amin11/C), C D Eb Bb Cmin9 (was A#add9Add11/C), C D Bb C7sus2 (was A#add9/C), C D Eb Gb A Cdim9 (was D7b9/C). A lone tritone reads out as two notes again.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: ScaleView Simple. A 200x100 icon showing the twelve pitch classes as circles, with the notes of the selected scale lit. ScaleView Pro without the chord detection: it does not read MIDI at all and never names a chord. The icon, the scales, the key-aware spelling, Simplify Note Names, the menus, the colours, the per-project scale and the toolbar toggle all behave exactly as they do in Pro.

version.author: kallums
version.changelog: Wording in the menus follows Apple's writing guidelines: "Random Scale" is now "Choose a Random Scale". Also the first release of the house colours since 1.0.3: a darker background, dark note names on lit circles, and White in place of Gold among the highlights.
